sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:164544
Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 37429 of 2021

Applicant :- Guruvendra
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Aradhna Chauhan,Anil Kumar Singh,Pankaj Kumar Shukla,Sanjeev Ku
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Lal Vijai Singh,Vinod Singh
Hon'ble Vikram D. Chauhan,J.
1.
Learned A.G.A. submits that instructions have been received and he has no objection in case the bail application is heard on merits.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.
The present bail application has been filed under Section 498A, 323, 504, 313 I.P.C and sections 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The applicant is the husband and the informant Smt. Ranjana Devi is the wife.

After filing of the present petition, learned counsel for the parties have taken effort for reconciliation between the husband and wife and in pursuance to the order dated 10.07.2023, a sum of Rs. 50,000/- has been paid to the wife by the husband.
The husband and wife both have appeared before the Court and have been identified by their respective counsels and have stated that they would live together peacefully.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant will keep his wife with dignity and ensures that rights of the wife shall not infringed.
The applicant was already released on interim bail vide order dated 10.07.2023.
The applicant has no previous criminal history.
In case he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

3A. It is to be seen that with the effort of counsel for the applicant Sri Pankaj Kumar Shukla, and counsel for the informant Sri Vinod Singh, the present matter has been reconciled between the Guruvendra vs State Of U.P. on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71340320/
1
husband and wife.
Learned counsel for the informant at this stage submits that he would have no objection in case, the bail is granted to the husband, provided, the husband keeps his wife with dignity.
4. Learned A.G.A. for the State submits that as the husband and wife have settled their dispute and want to live together, he would have no objection in case, bail is granted to the applicant.
5. Learned AGA has not brought any fact or circumstances to indicate criminal history or antecedents of the applicant which would disentitle the applicant for Bail.
6. It is not the case of the State that the applicant has not cooperated in the investigation or proceedings before the trial court.
7. The principle that Bail is a rule and Jail is an exception has been well recognised by Apex Court more specifically on the touch stone of Article 21 of the Constitution.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Apex Court in Satyendra Kumar Antil Vs Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA has not shown any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the Applicant.

8. No material, facts or circumstances has been shown by learned AGA that the accused may tamper with the evidence or witnesses or the accused is of such character that his mere presence at large would intimidate the witnesses or that accused will use his liberty to subvert justice or tamper with the evidence.
9.
It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA for the State.
10. Learned AGA for the State has not shown any material or circumstances that the accused/applicant is not entitled to bail in larger interests of the public or State.

11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, submissions of learned counsel for the parties, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case as well as the husband and wife have settled their dispute, the Court is of the view that a fresh opportunity be given to the couple to start a new journey the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
The bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant- Guruvendra involved in Case Crime No. 436 of 2020, under Sections 498A,
323, 504, 313 I.P.C and sections 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Khurja, District- Bulandshahr may appear before the court concerned within 30 days and the court concerned shall release the applicant on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions:-
Guruvendra
vs State Of U.P.

on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71340320/
2
(i). The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii).

The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted and/ or the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.
( iv).
The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v). The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(vi). The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court.
(vii). In the event, the applicant changes his residential address, he shall inform the court concerned about his new residential address in writing.

(viii). Applicant shall keep his wife with dignity and shall not indulge in any unlawful activity.
13.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
14. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the divorce petition has been withdrawn by the husband.

Considering the aforesaid submission of learned counsel for the applicant, a liberty is hereby granted to the applicant-husband as well as the wife-opposite party to file appropriate petition for quashing of the proceedings in accordance with law.
